org_full: NYC Mayor's Office of Contract Services

snippets.body: Lead procurement transformation by leveraging expertise, innovation, and a results-oriented mindset.
Equitable procurement through transparency, accountability, and efficiency.

The Mayor's Office of Contract Services (MOCS) is a New York City oversight and service agency that is dedicated to optimizing existing operations and transforming processes to make it easier to do business with the City.
Launched in 2017, the Procurement and Sourcing Solutions Portal (PASSPort) is New York City's end-to-end procurement platform
Anyone can browse public contract opportunities published in PASSPort
Launched in 2022, the PASSPort Public website provides public access to data and analytics, while promoting transparency and a deeper understanding of NYC's procurement activities.
Kim L. Yu is the City Chief Procurement Officer and New York City Mayor's Office of Contract Services (MOCS) Director.
Appointed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani in January 2026, she leads efforts to modernize procurement systems, increase transparency, and foster more equitable contracting across all city agencies.
snippets.attribution: NYC MOCS · Senior Team (Kim L. Yu) — https://www.nyc.gov/site/mocs/about/senior-team.page

snippets.body: MOCS staff operates in a fast-paced, collaborative, service-oriented environment, where flexibility and ability to achieve results are valued.
HSC's goal is to better the lives of all New Yorkers so they can reach their full human potential.

Section 4-06 of the Procurement Policy Board Rules (Rules) requires City agencies to process contract payments efficiently and expeditiously so as to assure timely contract payments to those suppliers doing business with the City.
An April snapshot of Procurement and Sourcing Solutions Portal (PASSPort) records for all contracts (not just non-profits) revealed over 7,000 pending unpaid invoices worth over $1 billion
the City entered into 12,820 new procurement and revenue contracts in FY 2023, valued at $38.22 billion

snippets.body: The Procurement Policy Board is authorized to promote and put into effect rules governing the procurement of goods, services, and construction by the City of New York.
Foster effective broad-based competition from all segments of the vendor community; including small businesses, minority and women-owned and operated enterprises
